scenario: Two submarine cable repair vendors, Vendor X and Vendor Y, are compared on fault-resolution success rates. Vendor X is disproportionately dispatched to major cable breaks (harder), whereas Vendor Y mostly handles minor faults.

data.description: Resolution success rates by fault severity

question: (a) Which vendor has the higher aggregate success rate? (b) Which vendor performs better within each fault-severity class? (c) Compute corrected rates using a 50/50 severity mix.

ground_truth.explanation: Vendor Y's higher aggregate reflects its lighter workload (mostly minor faults). Stratifying eliminates this confound and reveals Vendor X is superior at both severity levels.

naive_answer: Vendor Y is superior with an overall rate of 0.8971 vs Vendor X's 0.7871.
naive_trap: Fault severity is a confounder: minor faults inflate Vendor Y's aggregate because it handles six times more minor than major cases.
reasoning_trace: Major: X 0.76 > Y 0.70. Minor: X 0.95 > Y 0.93. X handles 85.7% major cases, dragging its aggregate. Corrected 50/50: X=0.5×0.76+0.5×0.95=0.855, Y=0.5×0.70+0.5×0.93=0.815. X wins.
python_verification:
nXm,rXm,nXn,rXn = 600,0.76,100,0.95
nYm,rYm,nYn,rYn = 100,0.70,600,0.93
ovX=(nXm*rXm+nXn*rXn)/(nXm+nXn); ovY=(nYm*rYm+nYn*rYn)/(nYm+nYn)
assert ovY > ovX
cX=0.5*rXm+0.5*rXn; cY=0.5*rYm+0.5*rYn
assert abs(cX-0.855)<0.005 and abs(cY-0.815)<0.005
assert cX > cY
